title: Contract Amendments and CapEx-to-OpEx Shift Procedure (Policy + Checklist) 2026
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Overview

Purpose
This document defines the standardized process for (1) assessing and approving contract amendments that change payment or delivery terms, and (2) handling transfers of capitalized project spend (CapEx) to operating expense (OpEx) when contracting or procurement events trigger a change in accounting treatment. The goal is to preserve revenue recognition integrity, maintain auditability, and provide a repeatable, cross-functional checklist for finance, legal, procurement, and engineering stakeholders.

Scope
Applies to: all Redwood contracts, purchase orders, and procurement commitments where either: a) the counterparty or contract amendment changes payment terms, milestones, or deliverables that impact timing of cash or revenue recognition; or b) procurement originally requested as capital expenditure is later reclassified to OpEx as a result of contract structure, term, or usage-based billing.

Definitions
- Amendment: any signed change to an executed contract that alters price, term, scope, or payment structure.
- CapEx-to-OpEx shift: the reclassification of previously anticipated capitalizable costs into operating expense based on contract use, contract term, or accounting guidance.
- Revenue Trigger Event: a contractual change that affects when revenue can be recognized (for example, shifting from milestone-based invoicing to usage-based invoicing).

When this doc should be invoked
- Legal proposes an amendment that extends a term, removes a milestone, or introduces a recurring/usage billing model.
- Procurement or engineering requests scope changes that convert a deployable asset into a hosted/subscription service.
- Account team renegotiates payment terms (e.g., prepay to net-60 or net-90).
- Finance identifies an existing PO or commitment that no longer meets capitalization criteria.

Policy (high-level)
- No contract amendment that materially affects revenue timing or capitalizability may be executed without completing the Contract Amendment & CapEx Review (CACR) checklist below.
- Ownership: Finance owns accounting treatment decisions and final sign-off on CapEx-to-OpEx reclassifications. Legal owns contract language and risk assessment. Procurement owns PO issuance and version control. Sales/account owners must initiate amendment requests and provide commercial context.

Approval Matrix (thresholds)
Use the following approval tiers for amendments and reclassification:

| Amendment or Reclassification Value | Required Approvals | Documentation Required | SLA to Decision |
|-------------------------------------|--------------------|------------------------|------------------|
| <= $50k                             | Account Manager + Procurement Lead | Signed amendment draft, CACR checklist | 5 business days |
| $50k - $250k                        | + Finance Manager | As above + impact revenue memo | 7 business days |
| $250k - $1M                         | + Head of Finance + Legal Counsel | As above + accounting memo + tax brief | 10 business days |
| > $1M                               | + CFO + General Counsel + Revenue Ops | Full financial model, audit trail, exec approval | 15 business days |

Step-by-step Procedure (numbered)
1. Initiation
   - Trigger: Account, Procurement, or Legal flags an amendment or a reclassification need.
   - Submit: Initiator fills the 'Amendment Request Form' (Confluence link) and attaches draft amendment, original contract, and PO/commitment.

2. Triage (Procurement)
   - Procurement verifies contract versions, PO numbers, and vendor details.
   - Assigns a procurement ticket and notifies Finance and Legal.

3. Financial Impact Assessment (Finance)
   - Determine if amendment changes: timing of invoicing, deliverables tied to milestones, capitalization criteria, or unlocks right-of-use assets.
   - If CapEx to OpEx is suspected, Finance completes the 'CapEx Reclassification Assessment' worksheet (spreadsheet template). Key fields: original capitalizable cost basis, remaining useful life, reason for reclassification, and expected P&L impact.

4. Legal Review (Legal)
   - Legal assesses risks, change in liability profile, termination rights, and ensures amendment language has clear billing and acceptance criteria.

5. Cross-Functional Decision (Finance + Legal + Procurement + Sales)
   - Convene if approval tier requires. Finance documents accounting expected treatment (capitalization vs. expense), and Revenue Ops assesses revrec impact (deferred revenue, milestone deferral, or immediate recognition).

6. Documentation and Approvals
   - Attach the completed CACR checklist, financial memos, and legal redlines to the procurement ticket.
   - Collect sign-offs per Approval Matrix. Obtain e-signature if required by policy.

7. Post-Approval Actions
   - If reclassification approved: Finance posts journal entries and updates fixed-asset or expense schedules.
   - Procurement issues updated PO or credit/debit notes.
   - Revenue Ops updates revenue forecasts and deferred revenue schedules.
   - Legal archives executed amendment and updates contract register.

8. Audit Trail and Closeout
   - All artifacts (forms, memos, approvals, accounting entries) must be archived in the contract folder (document management) and linked in the procurement ticket. Retain per retention policy (7 years).

CACR Checklist (condensed)
- [ ] Amendment draft attached and versioned
- [ ] Original contract & PO attached
- [ ] Initiator notes scope change and commercial rationale
- [ ] Finance impact worksheet completed
- [ ] Revenue Ops impact documented (deferred revenue or timing)
- [ ] Legal risk memo attached with redlines
- [ ] Approval signatures collected per Approval Matrix
- [ ] Journal entry or asset schedule updated (if applicable)
- [ ] Document stored in contract registry (link)

Accounting Treatment Guidance (practical examples)
1) Example: Milestone invoicing removed and replaced by monthly usage fees
   - Impact: revenue recognition likely shifts to over-time; may increase deferred revenue if prepayments remain. Finance must quantify remaining performance obligations and update revenue curves.
   - Suggested entry: move recognized revenue from milestone buckets to subscription revenue accounts across remaining term; adjust deferred revenue schedule.

2) Example: Capital procurement reclassified as OpEx because the item is a managed service rather than a company-owned asset
   - Impact: remove asset capitalization entry, reverse amortization schedules, and expense previously capitalized amounts to P&L in period of reclassification (unless guidance requires prospective treatment). Document tax implications.

Sample Journal (simplified)
- Reverse capitalization (one-time adjustment)
  DR Accumulated Depreciation - Equipment  120,000
  DR Loss on Reclassification               30,000
  CR Fixed Asset - Equipment               150,000

- Subsequent: expense recognized monthly as part of Hosting/Services expense

Revenue Recognition Notes
- Revenue Ops must re-evaluate the 'satisfaction of performance obligations' when contract scope or billing frequency changes.
- If an amendment increases the term but removes customer acceptance milestones, revenue may require recognition over time (ASC 606 principles).

Roles & Responsibilities (short)
- Finance: final accounting judgment, journal entries, financial memos, capital policy interpretation.
- Legal: contract language and risk acceptance; ensures amendment protects company interests.
- Procurement: ticketing, PO updates, supplier notifications, contract registry updates.
- Sales/Account: commercial rationale and customer negotiation context; ensures customer-signed amendment is uploaded.
- Revenue Ops: revenue modeling, deferred revenue schedules, and forecast adjustments.

Escalation Path
- Day 0-7: Procurement owner coordinates.
- If decision requires >7 business days, escalate to Head of Finance and Legal Counsel.
- For >$1M or material customer disputes, schedule an executive review with CFO and GC within 3 business days of escalation.

Appendix A: Amendment Request Template (text)
- Contract ID: __________
- Counterparty: __________
- Amendment summary: one-paragraph commercial description
- Reason for amendment: __________
- Value impact (ARR/One-time): __________
- Suggested accounting treatment: CapEx / OpEx / No change
- Business owner: __________

Appendix B: Quick Examples of Accepted Evidence
- Signed redline PDF with e-signature trace
- Accounting memo with calculations and reference GL codes
- Procurement ticket ID and PO change history

Notes for auditors
- All reclassifications must include a business justification and be signed by Head of Finance. Post-close adjustments will be labeled and retained as audit workpapers.
